title: The Hospital Gate
subtitle: A rumour of a hidden death brings families to the gate at midnight
coldOpen: 23:10. A patient dies after a six-hour wait in casualty.
23:40. A voice note says four more deaths are hidden.
Families crowd the gate; ambulances cannot turn in.

briefing.grievance: Families say the casualty ward makes people wait for hours and nobody tells them anything. One death tonight turned that into a rumour of many. They want the truth and a doctor who will talk.
knownFacts: One patient died at 23:10 after a six-hour wait; a medical review is required.
Casualty has two doctors for forty patients tonight.
Three ambulances are waiting outside the blocked gate.
unverifiedClaims: A voice note says four bodies are being hidden in a store room.
A post says relatives beat a doctor inside.
briefing.responsibility: You run the hospital’s night administration and police liaison. The gate must open for ambulances, and the families must get an honest account.
briefing.objective: Reopen the gate by agreement, tell the truth about the death, and get the ward the doctors it needs.

decisions.title: The gate
decisions.situation: Two hundred relatives are at the gate. Three ambulances are stuck. Inside, two doctors are treating forty people.

options.title: Bring the senior doctor to the gate to speak
options.preview: The duty consultant tells the families what happened and what is being done.
options.authority: Duty to hear grievances; Article 19(1)(a) free expression
options.consequence: The families hear a doctor, not a guard. The gate opens a lane for ambulances.

options.title: Announce the facts: one death, a review
options.preview: The night administrator reads the facts and promises a review by morning.
options.authority: Duty of candour: say what is known and what is not
options.consequence: The number is one, said aloud. The crowd argues less about numbers.

options.title: Clear the gate with police
options.preview: Officers push the relatives into the road.
options.authority: Article 19(2)–(3): restrictions must be reasonable and specific
options.consequence: The gate opens over grieving people. The voice note sounds truer than ever.

delayed.message: The crackdown hardens people who had stayed out of it. More arrive, angrier.

options.title: Keep the gate shut
options.consequence: A patient in the third ambulance gets worse.

decisions.title: The shoving starts

rightsMoments.question: Relatives are blocking a hospital gate after a death. What must the response respect?

options.text: The need to reopen access for ambulances with the least force, while keeping relatives informed and able to gather peacefully.
options.feedback: Correct. Life-saving access is urgent, but it is met by the least intrusive means, not by beating a grieving crowd.

options.text: Nothing; a hospital gate can be cleared by any means because lives are at stake.
options.feedback: Lives at stake justify urgency, not unlimited force; proportionality still applies.

options.text: Only the relatives’ wishes; ambulances must wait until they are satisfied.
options.feedback: Ambulance access is itself a matter of life; the duty is to reopen it by the least harmful route.

rightsMoments.principle: Article 21 protects life, which includes emergency access to care; Article 19 protects peaceful gathering. The state must secure access using the least force that works.
rightsMoments.why: A lane held by relatives themselves kept ambulances moving while the pushing group was isolated.

source.label: Constitution of India, Articles 21 and 22 (India Code)

simple.question: Grieving relatives block the hospital gate. What must the response respect?

options.a: Open a lane for ambulances gently, keep relatives informed and let them gather.
options.b: Anything goes. Lives are at stake.
options.c: Only the relatives’ wishes. Ambulances wait.

feedback.a: Yes! Open the lane the gentlest way, and keep talking.
feedback.b: No. Urgency does not allow unlimited force.
feedback.c: Ambulances carry lives too. Open the lane kindly, but open it.

simple.principle: Life comes first, which means ambulances get through. Use the gentlest way that works, and keep people informed.
simple.why: A lane held by relatives kept ambulances moving while the pushers were isolated.
